source: Hebrew Gospel of Luke v2.1 (Van Rensburg 2026, Vat. Ebr. 100)
method: Consonantal analysis — niqqud stripped, no English/Greek reference provided

verses.translation: And he said to his disciples: There was a certain rich man who appointed a steward [or: trustee] over his possessions, and a bad reputation [literally: evil name] went out against him — that he was squandering the master's [or: lord's] possessions. And he said to his disciples: It is an impossible thing that troubles [or: stumbling blocks] will not come, but woe to the one through whom they come.

translation_notes: אחד (H258 vs H259): H258 'to unify/collect thoughts' vs H259 'one'. In context 'a rich one' and 'a steward one' clearly call for the numeral/indefinite article 'one'. Chose H259.
היה (H1961 vs H1962): H1961 'to exist/be' vs H1962 'ruin'. 'A rich one was' makes sense as existence; 'ruin' does not fit. Chose H1961.
שם (H8033 'there' vs H8034 'name' vs H8035 'Shem' vs H8036 'name'): The phrase 'went out upon him a ___ evil' clearly calls for 'name/reputation' (שם רע = bad name). Chose H8034.
רע (H7451 vs H7452 vs H7453 vs H7454 vs H7455): Following שם, 'evil/bad' (H7451) produces the natural idiom 'bad name/reputation.' Chose H7451.
אבל (H56-H61): Most candidates relate to mourning or place names. H61 'nay, truly, yet/but' fits as a conjunction transitioning from 'troubles will come' to 'but woe.' Chose H61.
אוי (H188 vs H189): H188 'woe/lamentation' vs H189 a personal name. 'Woe to the one' is coherent. Chose H188.
הוא (H1931 vs H1933 etc.): Used as emphatic pronoun 'it is.' Chose H1931.
textual_notes: The word מורשה (H4181) typically means 'possession/inheritance' in biblical Hebrew; here it appears to be used in a later Hebrew sense of 'appointee/steward' — someone placed over possessions, i.e., an estate manager. This is a post-biblical semantic development.

The text appears to combine two distinct sayings: the parable of the steward (first sentence) and a saying about stumbling blocks (second sentence starting with ואמר לתלמידיו). The relationship between these two is unclear from the text alone.

verses.literal: And he said to his disciples a rich one was who made a steward one over his possessions and went out upon him a name evil that he was wasting the possessions of the lord. And he said to his disciples a thing not possible it [is] that not will come troubles but woe to whom that on account of him they will come.

verses.translation: And he called him and said to him: What is this that I am hearing about you? It would be more fitting [or: better] for him that a millstone be [hung] on his neck and he be cast into the sea, than if he should cause harm [or: do evil] to one of the little ones.

translation_notes: זה (H2088 vs H2089 vs H2090): H2088 'this' vs H2089 'a sheep'. 'What is this that I hear' is natural. Chose H2088.
שוה (H7737 vs H7738 vs H7739 vs H7740): H7737 'to level/equalize/to be fitting' vs H7738 'to destroy'. 'More fitting for him' makes perfect sense. Chose H7737.
בים (H3220 vs H3222): H3220 'sea' vs H3222 'warm spring'. Being cast into the sea with a millstone is the coherent image. Chose H3220.
רע (H7451 vs others): 'Does evil to one of the little ones' — H7451 'bad/evil' is the natural fit. Chose H7451.
שאם: ש (relative prefix) + אם (H518 'if') = 'than if.' H517 'mother' makes no sense here. Chose H518.
מן (H4480 vs others): 'From/out of the little ones' — partitive use. Chose H4480.
textual_notes: The text abbreviates שא״ני with abbreviation marks — likely שאני 'that I [am]'. The abbreviation dots suggest a scribal convention.

The transition between 'what is this that I hear about you' (addressing the steward) and the millstone saying (a general teaching about harming little ones) suggests a textual seam or combined traditions. It is unclear whether 'for him' refers to the steward or is a general pronoun.

verses.literal: And he called him and said to him what [is] this that I am hearing about you. More it would be fitting for him that would be a millstone on his neck and thrown into the sea than if he does evil to one from the little ones.
And the steward said in his inner-part what will I do that my lord is taking from me my authorization I do not know to dig shame there is to me to ask
verses.amplified: And the one entrusted [or: the steward, the authorized one] said within himself [in his heart]: What shall I do, since my lord is taking from me my authorization [or: my stewardship]? I do not know [how] to dig, and I have shame [or: am ashamed] to beg.
words: and the steward (the one entrusted with possession)
work: אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer (proper name)'. Chose H559 because the subject 'the steward' is performing speech, fitting the verb 'to say'.

והמורשה (consonants מורשה): H4181 'a possession'. In context, the prefix ה makes it 'the possession/steward' — one who holds a possession or authorization on behalf of another, i.e., a steward or authorized agent.

לשאול (consonants שאול): Candidates: H7585 'Sheol/the underworld', H7586 'Shaul (proper name)'. However, the consonants שאל also support the common verb 'to ask/beg' (H7592, not listed but the root is clear). Context demands 'to beg' — the steward is contrasting digging and begging as alternatives. Sheol or a proper name makes no sense here.
בושת (consonants בושת): The root בוש means shame/disgrace. The ת suffix forms a noun 'shame'. This fits: 'shame there is to me to beg.'
ambiguities: והמורשה: This word uses H4181 'possession' but in context functions as 'the one entrusted with possession' — a steward or authorized agent. The noun is being used to describe the person's role.
לשאול: The consonants could theoretically read 'to Sheol' (H7585) or 'to Saul' (H7586), but contextually this must be the infinitive 'to ask/beg' from the root שאל.
נוטל and הרשאתי are post-biblical Hebrew forms not found in Strong's classical lexicon; נוטל means 'taking/removing' and הרשאה means 'authorization/stewardship' in later Hebrew.

verses.literal: I do not know what I will do when I will be removed from the authorization in a manner that they will receive me in a house
verses.amplified: I know [now] what I will do, so that when I am removed from the stewardship [or: authorization], they will receive me into [their] houses.
work: מן (consonants מן): Candidates: H4478 'manna', H4480 'from/out of', H4482 'a musical chord'. Chose H4480 because 'from the authorization' fits the context of being removed from a position.
באופן (consonants אופן): H212 'a wheel'. In later Hebrew, אופן came to mean 'manner/way' (from the idea of a turning wheel). Context requires 'in a manner/so that'.
בבית (consonants בית): Candidates: H1004 'a house', H1006 'Bajith (place name)'. Chose H1004 because the steward wants to be received into someone's house/home.
ambiguities: איני יודע: The consonants read 'I do not know,' but the narrative logic suggests the steward has just devised his plan, so this may be a transitional statement meaning 'I know [what to do]' — the negation possibly belonging to the preceding thought rather than this sentence. Alternatively, this entire section is the steward's internal deliberation before the plan.
מסולק and ההרשאה are post-biblical Hebrew forms; מסולק is a passive participle meaning 'removed/dismissed' and הרשאה means 'authorization/stewardship'.

verses.literal: He called one one from the debtors of his lord and said to the first how much are you owing to my lord
verses.amplified: He called [them] one by one, from among those indebted to his lord, and said to the first: How much do you owe to my lord?
work: קרא (consonants קרא): Candidates: H7121 'to call out to', H7122 'to encounter', H7124 'a partridge'. Chose H7121 because the steward is summoning the debtors — an active calling.
אחד אחד: Both instances are H259 'one'. The repetition 'one one' is a distributive idiom meaning 'one by one' or 'each one'.
ואמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H563 'a lamb'. Chose H559 because this is direct speech following the calling of debtors.
כמה: Could be H3642 'to pine after' or a compound of כ + מה (H4100 'what/how much'). Chose the compound reading because 'how much?' is the natural interrogative before a debt amount.
אתה (consonants אתה): Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H859 'you'. Chose H859 because the steward is addressing the debtor directly: 'how much are you owing?'
ambiguities: ממחוייבי and חייב are post-biblical Hebrew legal terms for 'debtors' and 'owing/liable' respectively, not found in the classical Strong's lexicon.

verses.literal: And he answered him a hundred measures of oil and he said to him take your document and do quickly and write fifty
verses.amplified: And he answered him: A hundred measures of oil. And he said to him: Take your document [or: your bond], and do [it] quickly — and write fifty.
work: שמן (consonants שמן): Candidates: H8080 'to be oily', H8081 'oil/grease', H8082 'greasy/rich'. Chose H8081 because 'a hundred measures of oil' is a concrete commodity owed as a debt.
והוא (first and second instances): H1931 'he' — the pronoun functioning as subject. First instance: the debtor answers. Second instance: the steward speaks.
אמר: H559 'to say' — direct speech introducing the steward's command.
מהרה: Candidates: H4120 'promptly/hurry', H2029 'to be pregnant'. Chose H4120 because the steward urges speed in altering the document.
וכתב: Candidates: H3789 'to write', H3791 'a writing/document'. Chose H3789 because this is an imperative: 'and write fifty'.
חמ<ים: The < appears to be a textual corruption or abbreviation. The context demands 'fifty' (חמשים), which fits the narrative of reducing the debt from one hundred.
ambiguities: חמ<ים: The consonantal text appears damaged or uses an abbreviation. The < character suggests a missing consonant. In context, 'fifty' (חמשים) is the most coherent reading, as it represents a reduction from the hundred measures stated.
שטרך is a post-biblical Hebrew term for a legal document or bond, not found in the classical Strong's lexicon.
מדות could derive from מדה (H4060 'a measure') in its plural form, referring to units of liquid measurement.

verses.translation: And he said to another: How much have you been indebted to my master? And he said: A hundred measures of wheat. If not to suspect [or: to be suspicious] of the generous ones — but I, I am not... [text damaged]. And he said: Take your documents [letters] and write eighty.

translation_notes: אמר (all instances): Chose H559 'to say' — fits narrative dialogue throughout.

לאחר: Candidates: H309 'to delay', H310 'after/behind', H311 'after', H312 'another/next', H313 'Acher (name)'. Chose H312 — 'to another [debtor]' continues the steward's scheme of calling debtors one by one.
כמה: Candidates: H3642 'to pine after', H4100 'what?/how?'. Chose H4100 — כ+מה = 'how much?' Same interrogative as section 5.
והוא (both): Chose H1931 'he'.
מאה: Chose H3967 'a hundred'.
אם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 — conditional particle 'if'.
לא: Chose H3808 'not'.

אבל: Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'but/yet/truly'. Chose H61 — adversative conjunction 'but' introducing a contrasting thought.
אני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'ship/fleet'. Chose H589 — first person pronoun.
וכתב: Chose H3789 'to write'.
שמנים: H8084 'eighty'. Clear numeral.
textual_notes: The phrase אם לא לחשור לחשוד מהנדיבים אבל אני איני י is very difficult. It appears to be an editorial aside or internal comment: 'if not to suspect, to be suspicious of the generous ones — but I, I am not...' The text appears damaged at י (single letter yod), cutting off whatever the speaker was saying.
לחשור and לחשוד both appear to mean 'to suspect' — the doubling may be emphatic or may reflect textual corruption.
אותיותך 'your letters/documents' is a post-biblical Hebrew form (from אות 'sign/letter' + plural + 2ms suffix).
The ' mark again appears to be a scribal notation.

verses.literal: And he-said to-another how-much have-you-been-obligated to-my-master and-he said a-hundred measures wheat if not to-suspect to-suspect from-the-generous-ones but I I-am-not [damaged] and-he said take your-letters and-write eighty

verses.translation: And the master praised the dishonest [evil of heart] steward, because he had acted with shrewdness [wisdom]. For the sons of this world [age] are more clever [wise] in doing evil than the sons of good heart in their generation.

translation_notes: ושבח: Candidates: H7623 'to praise/commend loudly', H7624 'to adore'. Chose H7623 — 'praised/commended' fits the master commending the steward's shrewdness.
האדון: Candidates: H113 'sovereign/master/lord', H114 'Addon (name)'. Chose H113 — 'the master' who employed the steward.

רע: Candidates: H7451 'bad/evil', H7452 'crash/noise', H7453 'associate/friend', H7454 'thought', H7455 'badness'. Chose H7451 — 'evil' modifying 'the heart', describing the steward as 'evil of heart' (dishonest).
הלבב: Candidates: H3823 'to transport/stultify', H3824 'the heart', H3825 'the heart'. Chose H3824 — 'the heart' completing the phrase 'evil the heart' = 'evil of heart'.
כי: Chose H3588 — causal 'because/for'.
בחכמה: Candidates: H2451 'wisdom', H2452 'wisdom'. Chose H2451.
כן: Candidates: H3651 'thus/so/right', H3652 'so', H3653 'pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. Chose H3651 — adverb 'thus/so' transitioning to the moral.
זה: Chose H2088 'this' — demonstrative modifying 'the world'.
הם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 — pronoun 'they'.
להרע: The ל prefix + הרע (hiphil infinitive of רע). Candidates for רע: H7451 'evil', H7452 'crash', etc. Chose H7451 — 'to do evil' (causative form).
מבני: Candidates: H4012 'Mebunnai (name)', or מ + בני. Chose מ (from) + בני (sons of) — 'than the sons of', comparative.
טוב: Candidates: H2895 'to do good', H2896 'good', H2897 'Tob (place)', H2898 'goodness'. Chose H2896 — adjective 'good' modifying 'heart'.
לבב: Candidates: H3823 'to transport/stultify', H3824 'heart', H3825 'heart'. Chose H3824 — 'heart'.
textual_notes: רע הלבב could modify either המורשה ('the evil-hearted steward') or stand as a separate clause. Reading it as a construct phrase modifying the steward is more natural: 'the steward [who was] evil of heart'.
בדרו 'in his generation' — could also be read as בדרם 'in their generation' if the final vav is read differently, but the consonantal text shows בדרו (his generation).

verses.literal: And-praised the-master the-steward evil the-heart for in-wisdom he-did-it thus sons-of this the-world they [are] more wise to-do-evil than-sons-of good heart in-his-generation

verses.translation: And I say to you: Do not make for yourselves [friends] from the mammon [wealth] of evil heart [dishonest gain], so that when you come to nothing [are finished], they will gather you into everlasting dwellings [tents of perpetuity].
words: in order that / on account of

translation_notes: ואני: Chose H589 'I' — the speaker identifies himself.
שלא: ש (relative/that) + לא (H3808 'not') — 'that not' = prohibition.

הרוע: H7321 'to mar/break/shout'. Here הרוע functions as a noun 'the evil/the badness' (from רע + ה prefix). The form could be a hiphil infinitive construct 'the doing evil' or simply 'the evil'. Context of 'mammon of evil heart' = dishonest wealth.
לב: Candidates: H3820 'heart', H3821 'heart'. Chose H3820.
בעבור: Candidates: H5668 'on account of / in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 — purpose clause 'so that'.

באהלים: H174 'aloe wood sticks'. However, אהלים without the aloe-specific pointing would be the plural of אהל 'tent' (H168). Context demands 'tents/dwellings' — everlasting tents, not aloe wood sticks.
textual_notes: מממון is a loanword (Aramaic ממון 'wealth/mammon') not found in classical Strong's lexicon. It appears here in a clearly monetary/material context.
באהלים: The Strong's entry provided (H174 'aloe wood') shares consonants with אהלים 'tents' (plural of אהל H168). Context clearly demands 'tents/dwellings' — 'everlasting aloe sticks' makes no sense.

The phrase שלא תעשו לכם מממון הרוע לב is syntactically complex. It could mean 'do not make for yourselves [friends] from the mammon of evil heart' or 'do not make mammon of evil heart for yourselves.' The former reading, with an implied 'friends', fits the broader parable context better.
נצחיים is a post-biblical Hebrew adjectival form from נצח 'perpetuity/eternity'.

verses.literal: And-I saying to-you that-not you-shall-make for-you from-mammon the-evil heart in-order-that when-you-are ended they-will-gather-you in-tents everlasting

verses.translation: Whoever is faithful [trustworthy] in a small matter will be faithful in a great [matter]; and whoever is evil [untrustworthy] in a small matter will be evil in a great [matter].
words: in a matter / in a thing

translation_notes: מי (both): H4310 'who?' — indefinite 'whoever'.
שהוא: Chose H1931 'he' — relative clause 'that he [is]'.

בדבר / שבדבר: Candidates for דבר: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter/thing', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 — 'in a matter/thing' fits the comparison between small and great matters.
הוא: Chose H1931 'he' — pronoun in the second parallel clause.
רע (both): Candidates: H7451 'bad/evil', H7452 'noise', H7453 'associate', H7454 'thought', H7455 'badness'. Chose H7451 — 'evil/untrustworthy' as the opposite of נאמן 'faithful'.

verses.literal: Who that-he [is] faithful in-a-matter small in-a-great [matter] he-will-be faithful and who that-in-a-matter small he [is] evil in-a-great [matter] he-will-be evil

verses.translation: And if you have not been faithful [trustworthy] with what belongs to another [or: with what is genuine], who will entrust to you what is truly [your own]?

translation_notes: ואם (אם): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 because the clause structure 'and if not you were...' requires a conditional particle.
שהוא (הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1932 'he/it (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. ש+הוא = 'that is/which is'. Chose H1931 as the relative clause pronoun.

אמתי: Candidate: H573 'Amittai' (a proper name meaning 'my truth/genuine'). The consonants אמת+י naturally yield 'my truth' or 'true/genuine' as an adjective. In context, 'who that is true/genuine' makes sense as a description of something authentic, while the proper name Amittai would not fit this clause.
textual_notes: אמתי: The only Strong's entry is H573 (Amittai, a proper name), but the consonants אמת+י can also function as an adjective 'true/genuine' (from אמת, truth + adjectival suffix). Context strongly favors the adjectival reading rather than the proper noun.

The overall sense of the verse is somewhat compressed: 'if you were not faithful with what is genuine, who will give [it] to you?' — the referent of 'it' (the suffix on יגידהו) is unclear. יגידהו could mean 'will declare/tell it' or could be a broader sense of 'entrust/grant' depending on the root נגד.

verses.literal: And if not you-were faithful who that-is true who will-declare-it to-you

verses.translation: No person [or: human being] is able to serve two masters, for he will hate the one and love the other, or he will draw near [cling] to the one and despise the other. You are not able to serve YHWH and wealth [mammon].

translation_notes: שום: Candidates: H7760 'to put/place', H7761 same (Aramaic), H7762 'garlic'. In later Hebrew שום functions as 'any/no' (from the sense of 'placing/designating'). Context 'no human being is able' requires this quantifier reading. H7760 chosen as the base form.
אדם: Candidates: H119 'to be rosy', H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. 'No human being is able to serve' is the only coherent reading. Chose H120.
שני: Candidates: H8144 'crimson', H8145 'second/two'. 'Two masters' is natural and coherent; 'crimson masters' is not. Chose H8145.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'for/because'. The clause requires a causal conjunction. Chose H3588.
אל: Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H413 'to/near'. The verb יתקרב ('draw near') requires a directional preposition: 'draw near TO the one.' Chose H413.
האחד/והאחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one'. The article ה + אחד = 'the one', functioning as a pronoun in parallel pairs. Chose H259.
textual_notes: והממון: No Strong's entry provided for ממון. This is a loanword (mammon/wealth) common in later Hebrew and Aramaic but not in the classical Hebrew lexicon.

verses.literal: No human-being is-able to-serve two masters for he-will-hate the-one and-the-one he-will-love or he-will-draw-near to the-one and-the-one he-will-despise you-are-not able to-serve YHWH and-the-wealth

verses.translation: And the Pharisees [separatists], who were habituated [accustomed] to the trait of stinginess [greed], heard these words and poured out derision [mockery] upon him.

translation_notes: שהם: The ש is a relative particle ('who/that'). הם candidates: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance/wealth', H1992 'they'. 'Who they [were]' fits as a relative clause subject. Chose H1992.

אלה: Candidates: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to adjure/imprecate', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak/strong tree', H425 'Elah (name)', H426 'God'. However, אלה also commonly serves as the demonstrative pronoun 'these' (not listed separately here). In context 'these the-words' is clearly a demonstrative. Using H426 as a placeholder but noting this is the demonstrative 'these.'
לעג: Candidates: H3932 'to deride', H3933 'derision/scoffing', H3934 'buffoon/foreigner'. As an object of 'brought out,' the noun form 'derision/scoffing' (H3933) fits best.

במדת: The ב is preposition 'in'. מדת appears to be construct of מדה 'measure/trait' + דת could also be 'decree/law'. Context 'in the trait of stinginess' makes sense describing the Pharisees' character. Reading as מדת from מדה (measure/quality).
textual_notes: אלה: The demonstrative pronoun 'these' is the natural reading but was not listed among the candidates. The Strong's candidates all point to different words. The demonstrative אלה should probably be identified with a separate entry (sometimes catalogued under H428).
במדת: Could be parsed as ב+מדת (in the measure/trait of) or ב+מ+דת (in from the decree). The first parsing fits the context of describing a character trait.
מורגלים: No Strong's entry provided. This appears to be a passive participle from רגל in a denominative/causative sense 'to be accustomed/habituated', a usage common in later Hebrew.

verses.literal: And-the-Perushim who-they in-the-trait-of the-stinginess accustomed heard these the-words and-brought-out scoffing upon-him

verses.translation: And Yeshua said: You are the ones who justify [declare righteous] yourselves before people, but God knows your hearts, and what is great and exalted among people is small [insignificant] before God.

translation_notes: אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H562 same, H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer (name)'. Context 'And Yeshua said' clearly requires the verb. Chose H559.
הם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. 'You are they who justify yourselves' — the emphatic pronoun 'they' identifies the subject. Chose H1992.
רק: Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/but/merely', H7536 'spittle'. The adversative 'but' links the two contrasting clauses. Chose H7535.

האל (both occurrences): Candidates: H408/H409 'not', H410 'God/the Mighty', H411/H412 'these/those', H413 'to/near'. With the article ה, 'the God' (H410) is the natural reading in both places, as the sentence contrasts human judgment with divine knowledge. Chose H410.
ומה: Candidates: H4100 'what/how', H4101 same (Aramaic). Introduces the explanatory clause 'and what is great...' Chose H4100.
הוא (both): Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1932 same, H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Functions as copula 'it is' in both clauses. Chose H1931.
textual_notes: אתם: The only Strong's candidate is H864 'Etham (place name)'. This is clearly the second person plural pronoun 'you' (אתם), which should be identified separately from the place name.
The < symbol before הוא in the first occurrence may indicate a textual note or corruption in the manuscript.

verses.literal: And-Yeshua said you them the-ones-justifying yourselves before the-people but the-God knows your-hearts and-what [is] great and-exalted to-people small it [is] before the-God

verses.translation: The Law [royal decree] and the Prophets [were] until Yochanan [John], and after [that], the kingdom of God is being proclaimed [declared], and everyone is pressing [exerting force] into it.

translation_notes: עד: Candidates: H5703 'duration/perpetuity', H5704 'until/as far as', H5705 same (Aramaic), H5706 'booty', H5707 'witness', H5708 'menstrual flux'. 'Until Yochanan' is a temporal boundary marker. Chose H5704.
ואחר: Candidates: H309 'to loiter/delay', H310 'after/behind', H311 'after (Aramaic)', H312 'other/next', H313 'Acher (name)'. 'And after' as a temporal adverb following 'until Yochanan'. Chose H310.
האל: Candidates: H408/409 'not', H410 'God', H411/412 'these/those', H413 'to'. 'The kingdom of God' is the coherent reading. Chose H410.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1932 same, H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Serves as copula with the passive participle מוגד: 'it is declared.' Chose H1931.

מוגד: The candidates listed are for גד (H1407-H1410: coriander, Fortune, fortune, Gad). However, the מו- prefix suggests a hophal/passive participle from נגד ('to declare/proclaim'): מוגד = 'being declared/proclaimed.' This is not from the root גד but from נגד. Context strongly supports 'proclaimed.'
הכל: Candidates: H3605 'the whole/all', H3606 same (Aramaic). 'Everyone' as subject of 'making strength.' Chose H3605.
textual_notes: The opening ו לפני is syntactically odd — it could mean 'and before [there was only] the law and the prophets until Yochanan' or the ו could be a fragment. The sentence structure suggests the Law and Prophets operated as the framework until Yochanan, and afterward the kingdom of God is proclaimed.
מוגד: Parsed here as passive participle from נגד ('declare'), not from the root גד listed in the candidates. The מו- prefix is characteristic of the hophal stem.
חוזק: No Strong's candidates provided directly. From חזק ('to be strong/to seize/to press'). The phrase 'making strength in it' likely means 'pressing forcefully into it.'

verses.literal: And before the-law and-the-prophets until Yochanan and-after that-the-kingdom-of the-God it [is] declared and the-all making strength in-it

verses.translation: But it is easier [more likely] that the heavens [sky] and the earth will perish than [for] one letter [mark] of the Law to pass away and not be [fulfilled].

translation_notes: אבל: Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'truly/yet/but'. The adversative conjunction 'but' transitions from the previous statement. Chose H61.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1932 same, H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Copula 'it is.' Chose H1931.

מאות: Candidates: H225 'to come/assent', H226 'a sign/signal/mark'. The מ prefix = 'from/than'. אות = 'a sign/letter/mark.' 'Than one letter/mark of the law' — this refers to the smallest unit of the written law. Chose H226.
הדת: Candidates: H1881 'royal edict/statute', H1882 same. 'The law' — the same word used in section 5. Chose H1881.
ולא: Candidates: H3808 'not', H3809 same (Aramaic). Simple negation. Chose H3808.
textual_notes: ש<מים: The < symbol suggests a textual marker or possible corruption. The word appears to be שמים (heavens/sky) with a prefixed ש (that/which). The ש functions as a relative/conjunction: 'that heavens and earth will perish.'
מאות: Could be parsed as מ+אות ('than a sign/letter') or as מאות ('hundreds'). Context about the law not passing away strongly favors 'than a letter/sign of the law.'

verses.literal: But more easy it [is] that-heavens and-earth will-perish than-a-letter-of the-law one that-will-pass and-not will-be

verses.translation: Every person who abandons [divorces] his wife and takes [brings in] another commits adultery.

translation_notes: אדם: Candidates: H119 'to be rosy', H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. 'Every human being who leaves his wife' — clearly a person. Chose H120.
כל: Candidates: H3605 'the whole/all/every', H3606 same (Aramaic). 'Every' as a universal quantifier. Chose H3605.

verses.literal: Every human-being who-leaves his-wife and-brings another makes adultery

verses.translation: A certain man [who was] rich was clothed [dressed] in purple [fine garments] and feasting every day in abundance [luxury, goodness].

translation_notes: אדם: Candidates: H119 'to be rosy', H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. A person is being described. Chose H120.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. 'A certain man' — indefinite article use. Chose H259.
היה: Candidates: H1961 'to exist/become', H1962 'ruin'. 'Was' — past tense copula. Chose H1961.
לבוש: Candidates: H3830 'a garment', H3831 same, H954 'to be ashamed' (from בוש). 'Clothed in purple' — the garment/clothing sense is natural. Chose H3830.
בטוב: Candidates: H2895 'to be/do good', H2896 'good (adj)', H2897 'Tob (place)', H2898 'goodness/the best'. Preposition ב + noun = 'in goodness/luxury/abundance.' Chose H2898.

verses.translation: And there was a certain poor [weak, lowly] man whose name [was] Lazar [Eleazar, 'God helps'], lying at his doorway, stricken [afflicted] with sores [ulcers].

translation_notes: והיה: Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin'. 'And there was' — narrative past. Chose H1961.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one'. 'A certain poor man.' Chose H259.

לעזר: Candidates: H5826 'to protect/aid', H5827 'Ezer (name)', H5828 'aid', H5829 'Ezer (name)'. This is the personal name לעזר (Lazar, short for אלעזר 'God helps'). The root is עזר 'help/aid.' Chose H5828 as the base meaning, though this functions as a proper name.
שחין: Candidates: H7822 'inflammation/ulcer', H2433 'beauty' (from חין). A person lying at a door 'stricken with ulcers' is coherent; 'stricken with beauty' is incongruous. Chose H7822.

מוכה: The candidates listed are for כה (H3541 'thus/here', H3542 same). However, מוכה is clearly a passive participle from נכה ('to strike/smite'): 'stricken/smitten.' Context of being afflicted with boils confirms this.
textual_notes: ש<מו: The < symbol again appears to mark a textual note. The word is שמו ('his name').
לעזר: Could be the preposition ל + עזר ('for help') or the proper name לעזר (Lazar/Lazarus). Context 'his name [was] Lazar' clearly indicates a proper name.

verses.literal: And-there-was a-poor-one one his-name Lazar lying at-his-door stricken [with] boils

verses.translation: And he longed [desired] to be satisfied [filled] from the crumbs falling from the table of the rich man, but [he] would not give to him. And the dogs would come and lick his sores.

translation_notes: לשבוע: Candidate: H7620 'a week (sevened).' However, the consonants שבע also yield the verb שבע 'to be satisfied/sated/filled' (H7646). In context, 'he desired to be filled from crumbs' is coherent; 'he desired a week from crumbs' is not. Reading as the infinitive of שבע 'to be satisfied.'

באים: Candidate: H366 'frightful' (from אים). However, באים is naturally parsed as ב+אים or more likely the participle of בוא 'to come' (באים = 'coming/arriving'). 'The dogs coming and licking' is a coherent physical image. Chose the participle of בוא (H935).
מ<ולחן: The < symbol marks a textual note. The word is משלחן or מהשלחן ('from the table of'). שלחן = 'table' (H7979).
textual_notes: לשבוע: The only Strong's candidate listed is H7620 'week,' but the consonants clearly support שבע 'to be satisfied' (H7646), which fits the narrative. The infinitive construct with ל ('to be filled') is the natural reading.

ואינו נותן לו: This clause is ambiguous — it could mean 'and he [the rich man] was not giving to him' or possibly 'and there was no one giving to him.' The singular form אינו suggests a specific subject (the rich man).
מפירורין: No Strong's entry. This appears to be a later Hebrew/Aramaic form meaning 'crumbs' (from the root פרר 'to break/crumble').

verses.literal: And-he-desired to-be-satisfied from-crumbs the-falling from-the-table-of the-rich-one and-he-was-not giving to-him and-the-dogs coming and-licking his-boils

verses.translation: And the poor [or: lowly, weak] man died and they carried him to the throne [or: seat of honor] of Abraham and the rich man died and was buried

translation_notes: בכסא (כסא): Candidates: H3677 'fullness/full moon/festival', H3678 'throne/covered seat'. Chose H3678 because being carried to a throne/seat of honor after death fits the narrative of the poor man being elevated to Abraham's honored presence, whereas a moon festival makes no contextual sense.
textual_notes: ומת could theoretically be parsed as 'and a man' (H4962 plural form) but the narrative context with ונקבר (and was buried) strongly indicates this is the verb מות (to die) in a completed form, which shares the same consonants though not listed as a candidate. The text clearly intends 'and died' given the burial context.

verses.literal: And died the poor [one] and they carried him to [the] throne [of] Abraham and died the rich [one] and was buried

verses.translation: In Gehinnom [the valley of torment] and as he stood in anguish [or: suffering, smallness] and affliction he lifted up his eyes and saw from a distance Abraham and Lazar [Eliezer, 'my God is help'] in his place

translation_notes: בצער (צער): Candidates: H6819 'to be small/ignoble (fig. distress)', H6820 'Tsoar, a place'. Chose H6819 because the context describes suffering in Gehinnom, making 'distress/anguish' the coherent reading; a place name east of Jordan makes no sense here.

נשא (נשא): Candidates: H5375 'to lift', H5376 'to lift', H5377 'to lead astray/delude', H5378 'to lend on interest'. Chose H5375 because 'lifted his eyes' is a natural Hebrew idiom for looking up, fitting the scene of seeing Abraham from afar.

וראה (ראה): Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'a vulture', H7202 'experiencing', H7203 'a seer/vision', H7204 'Roeh (name)'. Chose H7200 because the verb 'to see' directly follows 'lifted his eyes,' forming the standard Hebrew phrase for observing something.

ולעזר (עזר): Candidates: H5826 'to aid/protect', H5827 'Ezer (name)', H5828 'aid', H5829 'Ezer (name)'. This is a proper name in context — the poor man mentioned earlier. The consonants ל+עזר with prefix ו suggest 'and Lazar/Elazar' — a personal name meaning 'God is [my] help.' Using H5828 as the root meaning behind the name.
textual_notes: ונגישה appears to be from the root נגש (to oppress/drive/exact), with a feminine noun suffix. It could mean 'oppression' or 'exaction.' Without a Strong's candidate provided, I read it as a noun meaning 'affliction/oppression' based on the consonants.
ולעזר could be read as 'and to Ezer' (a proper name) or as 'and Lazar' (a shortened form of Elazar). The context of a named poor man alongside Abraham supports a proper name reading.

verses.literal: In Gehinnom and in his standing in distress and oppression he lifted his eyes and saw from afar Abraham and Lazar in his place

verses.translation: And he cried out and said Abraham have mercy [or: show compassion] upon me and send to me Lazar [that] with his finger dipped [or: immersed] in water at the far [or: hinder] side he might cool my tongue for I am being oppressed [or: tormented] in flames of fire

translation_notes: ואמר (אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say', H561 'something said', H562 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer (name)'. Chose H559 because this is clearly a speech verb following 'he cried out.'

חמול (חמול): Candidate: H2538 'Chamul, an Israelite name.' However the consonants חמל are the root for 'to have compassion/spare' (חמל H2550). The text uses this as an imperative verb meaning 'have compassion!' The only listed candidate is the proper name, but the context demands the verbal meaning from the same root.

עלי (עלי): Candidates: H5940 'a pestle', H5941 'Eli (name)', H5942 'high', H5943 'supreme/God'. However, in context this is clearly the preposition על (H5921 'upon') with 1cs suffix -י, meaning 'upon me.' None of the listed candidates fit, but H5921 with suffix is the correct parsing.

ושלח (שלח): Candidates: H7971 'to send away/for/out', H7972 'to send', H7973 'a spear/branch', H7974 'Shelach (name)', H7975 'Shiloach (place)'. Also לח candidates H3892 'fresh', H3893 'vigor'. Chose H7971 because 'send to me Lazar' is a coherent request in this dialogue.

הטבול (טבול): Candidate: H2871 'dyed, a turban.' The consonants טבל also relate to the root meaning 'to dip/immerse' (H2881). In context, 'dipped in water' is the coherent image — a finger dipped in water to cool a tongue. The turban reading makes no sense here.
במים: Candidates: H4325 'water' vs H3220/H3221/H3222 'sea/warm spring.' Chose H4325 because 'water' is the natural reading for dipping a finger.
בצד (צד): Candidates: H6654 'a side', H6655 'at the side of.' Chose H6654 — 'at the side.'
כי (כי): Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction: for/because/that.' Chose H3588 because this introduces the reason for the plea.
אני (אני): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet.' Chose H589 because 'I am oppressed' is the coherent subject.
אש (אש): Candidates: H784 'fire', H785 'fire', H786 'there is/are', H787 'a foundation.' Chose H784 because 'flames of fire' is the coherent image of torment.
textual_notes: חמול is listed only as H2538 (a proper name Chamul), but contextually this must be an imperative from the root חמל meaning 'have compassion/spare.' The same consonants support both readings.
בצד האחור is unusual — 'at the side of the back/hinder part.' This may refer to the tip/back of the finger, or could be an unusual way of saying 'the far side.' The meaning is somewhat obscure.

לשוני: The provided candidates H7764/H7765 are for 'Shuni' — a proper name. But the consonants לשון+י clearly read as 'my tongue' (לשון H3956 + 1cs suffix). The candidate list appears incomplete here.
נגוש appears to be a passive participle from נגש (to oppress/exact), meaning 'I am being oppressed/tormented.' No candidate was provided but the root is clear from context.

verses.literal: And he cried out and said Abraham have compassion upon me and send to me Lazar with his finger the dipped in water at the side of the back let him cool my tongue for oppressed [am] I in flames of fire

verses.translation: And he said to him remember that you had abundant [or: great] good in your lifetime and Lazar had an abundance of misfortunes [or: evils, troubles] and now Lazar [is] in strength [or: comfort, firmness] and you [are] in anguish [or: distress]

translation_notes: זכור (זכור): Candidates: H2138 'a male', H2139 'Zakkur (name).' However the consonants זכר are the root for 'to remember' (H2142), and זכור is the infinitive absolute/imperative form. In context ('remember that you had good...') the verbal reading is demanded. Using H2138 as placeholder but the meaning is clearly 'remember.'
שהיה (היה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Jah.' Chose H1961 because 'that there was to you' is a standard Hebrew construction for possession.
רב (רב): Candidates: H7227 'abundant', H7228 'archer', H7229 'abundant', H7230 'abundance.' Chose H7227 because 'abundant good' describes the rich man's former life.
טוב (טוב): Candidates: H2895 'to be good', H2896 'good (adj/noun)', H2897 'Tob (place)', H2898 'goodness/the best.' Chose H2896 as the noun/adjective 'good' modifying the rich man's life.

רעות (רעות): Candidates: H7468 'a female associate', H7469 'a feeding upon/grasping after', H7470 'desire.' The consonants רעות also relate to רעה meaning 'evil/misfortune' (plural construct). Chose H7469 in the sense of troubles/afflictions, as the contrast with 'good' demands 'evils/misfortunes.'
ואתה (אתה): Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 'to arrive', H859 'you.' Chose H859 because 'and you are in distress' completes the contrast with Lazar.
בצער (צער): Candidates: H6819 'to be small/ignoble (distress)', H6820 'Tsoar (place).' Chose H6819 for 'distress' — the same word used in section 2 describing the rich man's torment.
textual_notes: בחוזק: No candidates were provided. The root חזק means 'strength/firmness' (H2392/H2393). In context this contrasts with בצער (distress), suggesting 'in comfort/strength/security.'
רעות could mean 'evils/misfortunes' (from רע) or 'strivings/vexations' (H7469). Both fit the contrast with 'good' but with slightly different nuances.

verses.literal: And he said to him remember that there was to you much good in your life and to Lazar there was in abundance of evil and now Lazar [is] in strength and you [are] in distress

verses.translation: And in [or: with] all these things [or: matters] between you and between him a great chasm [or: confusion, upheaval] is fixed [or: planted firmly] on account of this those who desire to cross over from here to you will not be given the ability to cross over here

translation_notes: אלה (אלה): Candidates: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to adjure/imprecate', H423 'an imprecation', H424 'an oak', H425 'Elah (name)', H426 'God.' However, the consonants אלה most commonly serve as the demonstrative pronoun 'these' (H428). None of the listed candidates exactly match, but contextually 'these things/matters' is the only coherent reading. Using H426 as placeholder.
בעבור (עבור): Candidates: H5668 'transit/on account of/in order that', H5669 'stored grain.' For the first occurrence chose H5668 'on account of' as it introduces the reason.
לעבור (עבור): For the second and third occurrences, the same consonants function as the infinitive 'to cross over' (from עבר H5674). H5668 is used as the closest match from candidates provided.
זה (זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that.' Chose H2088 because 'on account of this' is the natural reading.
להם (להם/הם): Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they.' Chose H1992 as the pronoun 'them' with preposition ל — 'to them.'
פה (פה): Candidates: H6310 'mouth', H6311 'here.' Chose H6311 because 'to cross over here' completes the spatial reference of the passage.
textual_notes: מהומה (H4103 'confusion/uproar') is used here to describe what separates the two realms. This seems to function as 'a great gulf/chasm' — the Hebrew word literally means 'tumult/confusion' but in context describes a barrier or divide.

תקועה: No candidates provided. The root תקע means 'to thrust/drive/fix firmly' (H8628). As a feminine passive participle it means 'fixed/established/planted.' This describes the barrier as permanently set.
שחפצין contains the root חפץ (to delight in/desire) with what appears to be a participial plural ending -ין (possibly Aramaic-influenced). This is a late Hebrew or mixed form.
מכאן: Listed candidate H575 'where/whither' for אן. However מכאן is a compound meaning 'from here' (מ + כאן). This is a post-biblical Hebrew form.

verses.literal: And in all these the things between you and between him [a] confusion great it [is] fixed on account of this those who desire to cross from here to you not will be given to them ability to cross here

verses.translation: And he said if so [or: if that is the case] would that [or: I entreat] you would send him to the house of my father

translation_notes: והוא (הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist.' Chose H1931 because 'and he said' is the natural reading introducing the rich man's speech.
אמר (אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say', H561 'something said', H562 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer.' Chose H559 as the verb 'said.'
אם (אם): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether.' Chose H518 because 'if so' is a conditional introduction.
כן (כן): Candidates: H3651 'so/thus/right', H3652 'so', H3653 'a stand/pedestal', H3654 'a gnat.' Chose H3651 because 'if so' is the natural conditional phrase.
אחלי (אחלי): Candidates: H304 'Achlai (name)', H305 'would that!' Chose H305 because 'would that you send him' is an entreaty fitting the rich man's plea.
לבית (בית): Candidates: H1004 'a house/family', H1005 'house', H1006 'Bajith (place)', H3487 'sign of object.' Chose H1004 because 'house of my father' means the father's household.
אבי (אבי): Candidate: H21 'Abi (name).' However the consonants אב+י clearly mean 'my father' (אב H1 + 1cs suffix). Using H21 as placeholder but the meaning is 'my father.'

verses.literal: And he said if so would that you would send him to [the] house of my father

verses.translation: For five brothers I have and he will warn [or: tell] them that they not come to the torment [or: oppression] of this place

translation_notes: כי (כי): Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction: for/because.' Chose H3588 as the causal conjunction introducing the reason for the request.
להם (להם/הם): Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they.' Chose H1992 — pronoun 'them' with preposition ל, 'to them.'
שלא (לא): Using H3808 'not' — the ש prefix functions as the relative/subordinating particle 'that,' making שלא = 'that not.'
המקום (מקום/קום): Candidates: H4725 'a place/standing', H6965 'to rise', H6966 'to rise.' Chose H4725 because 'this place' refers to the place of torment.
הזה (הזה/זה): Candidates: H1957 'to dream', H2088 'this/that', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this/that.' Chose H2088 because ה+זה = 'this' as a demonstrative modifying 'the place.'
textual_notes: חמ<ה: The text has an unusual character (<) which may indicate a damaged or uncertain letter. The context (a number of brothers) suggests חמשה (five), with the ש possibly damaged or abbreviated.
לנגישת: No candidates provided. This appears to be from the root נגש meaning 'oppression/exaction' (noun form with construct suffix -ת). It describes the torment of this place.

verses.literal: For five brothers there are to me and he will say to them that not they will come to [the] oppression of the place this
And Abraham said to him to them he [is] Moses and the prophets and let them hear them
verses.amplified: And Abraham said to him: They have Moses and the prophets — let them hear [or: listen to] them.
work: אמר: H559 'to say' — Abraham is speaking in response to a request.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', or ל + הם H1992 'to them'. Chose the prepositional compound 'to them' because Abraham is directing attention to what 'they' (the living) already possess.
הוא: H1931 'he/it' — functioning here as a copula: 'there is [for them]' Moses and the prophets.
משה: Candidates: H4871 'to pull out', H4872 'Moses', H4874 'a debt'. Chose H4872 because 'Moses and the prophets' is a recognizable reference to authoritative teaching/scripture.
ambiguities: The phrase להם הוא משה is syntactically ambiguous: it could mean 'to them there is Moses' (i.e., they have Moses) or 'he said to him: to them [belongs] Moses.' The overall sense is the same — the living already have access to Moses and the prophets.
והנביאים uses the standard Hebrew plural with the article; נביא (prophet) is well-established but not among the provided candidates.

verses.literal: And he said no Abraham but if some from the dead will go to them they will do repentance
verses.amplified: And he said: No, Abraham! But if some of the dead go to them, they will repent [or: turn back, do repentance].
work: אבל: Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'a meadow', H61 'nay/truly/yet'. Chose H61 because the speaker is making a contrastive statement: 'No... but if...'
אם: Candidates: H517 'a mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 because this introduces a conditional clause.
מקצת: H7117 'a portion/some'. Fits as 'some of the dead.'
להם: Prepositional compound ל + הם H1992 'to them' — the dead would go to the living.
הם: H1992 'they' — the living, the subject of the repentance.
תשובה: H8666 'a return/recurrence/reply'. In later Hebrew this word took on the specific meaning of 'repentance' (turning back to God). Context demands this meaning.

יעשו: Listed candidate H3299 'Jaasu (a proper name)' does not fit. This is clearly the 3rd person plural imperfect of עשה (H6213) 'they will do/make'. The Strong's entry for the proper name is irrelevant here.
ambiguities: יעשו: The only listed candidate is H3299 'Jaasu' (a proper name), but this is clearly a verb form — 3rd person masculine plural imperfect of עשה 'to do/make'. The provided candidates are inadequate here.
תשובה (H8666) literally means 'a return' or 'a reply' but functions in later Hebrew as 'repentance.' Both senses may be active: they will make a turning-back.

verses.literal: And Abraham said no if not they will hear Moses and the prophets and if one from the dead will return alive not they will believe
verses.amplified: And Abraham said: No — if they do not hear [or: listen to] Moses and the prophets, even if one from the dead returns alive, they will not believe.
work: אמר: H559 'to say' — Abraham responds with a definitive statement.
אם (first): H518 'if' — introducing the conditional: 'if they do not hear.'
ואם (second): H518 'and if' — introducing the second, more extreme conditional.
אחד: H259 'one' — referring to a single person from the dead.
משה: H4872 'Moses' — consistent with the previous section's reference to Moses and the prophets.
חי: Candidates: H2416 'alive/living', H2417 'alive (Aramaic)'. Chose H2416 because 'returns alive' describes resurrection in Hebrew.
ambiguities: מהנביאים: The consonants read 'from the prophets' (מן + הנביאים), but the narrative context (paralleling section 6's 'from the dead') strongly suggests this should read מהמתים 'from the dead.' This may be a scribal error, or the text intentionally says 'from the prophets' — meaning one of the dead prophets returning. Both readings are plausible; if 'from the prophets' is correct, it narrows the scope to a dead prophet returning alive.
The brackets ] [ at the end suggest damaged or missing text in the manuscript.
יחזור is a post-biblical Hebrew form meaning 'will return/come back,' not found in the classical Strong's lexicon.
